words.def: devoted to fine food and refined pleasure
words.ex: The chef prepared an epicurean feast of seven delicate courses.

words.def: the pursuit of pleasure as the most important goal in life
words.ex: The fable warns that pure hedonism leaves a person empty.

words.def: to spoil or weaken the quality of something
words.ex: One false fact can vitiate an entire argument.

words.def: so light and thin that you can almost see through it
words.ex: Diaphanous curtains let the morning light into the room.

words.def: the restoring of friendly relations between rivals
words.ex: The summit led to a rapprochement between the old rivals.

words.def: angry and bitter in speech or debate
words.ex: The meeting turned acrimonious when budgets came up.

words.def: harsh public criticism and abuse aimed at someone
words.ex: The scientist endured years of obloquy before her theory was accepted.

words.def: cool self-control in a dangerous or tense situation
words.ex: The pilot's sangfroid during the storm reassured every passenger.

words.def: producing the result that was wanted
words.ex: Rest proved more efficacious than any medicine.

words.def: stubbornly applying a theory without regard for practical results
words.ex: The doctrinaire planner would not change his design even when it failed.

words.def: pleasing to the ear
words.ex: The poet chose euphonious names for the rivers in her imaginary land.

words.def: very small in amount; barely enough
words.ex: The exiguous rations lasted the sailors only three days.

words.def: a philosophy holding that people create meaning through their own free choices
words.ex: The novel's hero turns to existentialism after realizing no one will hand him a purpose.

words.def: lying flat on your back, face up
words.ex: The patient lay supine on the table.

words.def: a short, formal statement of a rule or principle
words.ex: The coach's favorite dictum was that practice beats talent.

words.def: lacking self-control; going to extremes
words.ex: His intemperate remarks got him banned from the forum.

words.def: moving from place to place, never settling for long
words.ex: The peripatetic photographer lived out of a suitcase.

words.def: pure and complete, not mixed with anything else
words.ex: The news of the rescue brought unalloyed joy to the family.

words.def: holding firmly to a purpose and refusing to give up
words.ex: The pertinacious reporter called the mayor's office every day for a month.

words.def: honest and sincere, without any trickery
words.ex: Her guileless smile made everyone trust her immediately.

words.def: sharp, sour and witty in a cutting way
words.ex: Her acerbic wit made the talk show funny, though some guests left stung.

words.def: the part of metaphysics that asks what kinds of things exist and what it means to exist
words.ex: The professor's lecture on ontology asked what it means for a number to exist.

words.def: showing dedication and steady care
words.ex: The sedulous gardener tended each rose every morning.

words.def: the complete body of work of an artist or writer
words.ex: Her oeuvre includes twelve novels and two plays.

words.def: demanding immediate obedience without discussion
words.ex: The officer's peremptory command silenced the room.

words.def: the belief that life has no meaning and nothing has real value
words.ex: The villain's nihilism made him impossible to bargain with.

words.def: to announce a law or idea officially to the public
words.ex: The council will promulgate the new rules next week.

words.def: a formal public speech or written tribute praising someone at length
words.ex: The retirement dinner featured a panegyric for the beloved coach.

words.def: to make something deliberately confusing or hard to understand
words.ex: The contract seemed written to obfuscate the extra fees.

words.def: just begun and not yet fully formed
words.ex: She had only an inchoate idea for her science project.

words.def: a person who speaks several languages
words.ex: The polyglot guide switched between five languages.

words.def: the highest or most successful point
words.ex: The empire reached its apogee under its third ruler.

words.def: happening after a meal
words.ex: Grandpa always took a postprandial nap in his armchair.

words.def: clever but false reasoning, especially about moral questions
words.ex: The lawyer's casuistry made cheating sound almost noble.

words.def: a person who takes great pleasure in fine food and drink
words.ex: The epicure could name every spice in the stew.

words.def: to uproot someone from their home or culture
words.ex: War can deracinate whole families and scatter them across the world.

words.def: a trickster who fools people to get their money
words.ex: The traveling mountebank sold bottles of colored water as medicine.

words.def: impossible to escape or avoid
words.ex: Winter's arrival felt ineluctable as the days grew shorter.

words.def: naive and simplistic; also dull
words.ex: His jejune view of politics ignored how compromise works.

words.def: bad-tempered and spiteful
words.ex: His splenetic letter to the editor attacked everyone in town.

words.def: a nickname
words.ex: The fast runner earned the sobriquet Lightning.

words.def: returning to a very old, primitive way of acting or feeling
words.ex: Fear of the dark is an atavistic instinct left over from our distant ancestors.

words.def: focused entirely on oneself and one's own experience
words.ex: His solipsistic diary never mentions another person.

words.def: grumpy and irritable, as if from a sour stomach
words.ex: The dyspeptic critic disliked nearly every show he saw.

words.def: the opening part of a speech or essay
words.ex: The exordium grabbed the audience with a startling question.

words.def: light, playful teasing talk
words.ex: The friends' persiflage kept the long drive cheerful.

words.def: hairy or shaggy
words.ex: The hirsute mountain man had not trimmed his beard in years.

words.def: being a cheap, inferior substitute for the real thing
words.ex: The ersatz leather jacket peeled after one rain.

words.def: aiming to bring peace and calm disagreement
words.ex: The pastor wrote an irenic letter to heal the church's quarrel.

words.def: a person skilled at telling stories
words.ex: My uncle, a natural raconteur, kept the campfire crowd laughing.

words.def: a person who loves luxury and comfort
words.ex: The sybarite spent hours in his marble bath.

words.def: stubbornly disobedient to authority
words.ex: The contumacious witness refused every order from the judge.

words.def: deep wisdom and good judgment
words.ex: Villagers came from miles away to ask the old woman for advice, trusting her sagacity.
